'''E. R. C. Davidar''' ({{langx|ta|ஈ. ஆர். சி. டேவிதார்}}) was an Indian naturalist, scholar and lawyer. He is remembered for the first survey of the Nilgiri [[tahr]] in 1975 over western ghat range, conducting the first study in India on elephant corridors and taking an active part in the protection of the [[Nilgiri Mountains|Nilgiris]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-12-29 |title=Project to protect Nilgiri Tahr, Tamil Nadu animal, launched |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chennai/project-to-protect-nilgiri-tahr-tamil-nadu-animal-launched/articleshow/96588874.cms |access-date=2024-10-07 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

==Earlier days ==
He became interested in wildlife through hunting in Uthagamandalam and Coonoor.<ref name="thehindu2">{{cite news |title=Hunter turned protector |url=https://www.thehindu.com/features/magazine/Hunter-turned-protector/article16372208.ece |access-date=7 October 2024 |agency=The Hindu}}</ref> Before banning hunting in India via [[Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972|Wildlife Protection Act of 1972]], He enlisted the cooperation of the licensed hunters. Later he turned to conserve wildlife. In 1963, he studied the status of the Nilgiri [[tahr]]. In 1975 he published the detailed survey of Tahr in the Journal of the [[Bombay Natural History Society|Bombay Natural History Association]]. The animal then entered into the Red Data Book of the International Union for Conservation of Nature and plans.<ref name="thehindu2"/>

He was the secretary of the Planters’ Association in the Nilgiris and a member of various conservation organizations.<ref name="thehindu1">{{cite news |title=Understanding the Nilgiri tahr: Scientists all set to study Tamil Nadu's State animal |url=https://www.thehindu.com/life-and-style/understanding-the-nilgiri-tahr-scientists-all-set-to-study-tamil-nadus-state-animal/article67474423.ece |access-date=7 October 2024 |agency=The Hindu}}</ref> He has published several books including notable works like '' Whispers from the Wild: Writings by E.R.C. Davidar'' and ''Cheetal Walk: Living in the Wilderness''. He has also published stories for children and guidebooks on wildlife sanctuaries. After his retirement in 1981, he devoted his time for wild life conservation. He founded Sigur Nature Trust in June 2005.<ref>{{cite web |title=Founders |url=https://www.sigurnaturetrust.org/founders/ |website=Sigurnature Trust |access-date=7 October 2024}}</ref> He passed in April 2010 in puducherry.<ref name="thehindu2"/>

==Remembrance==
For his contribution to wildlife conservation, the Hall of Fame of the [[Tamil Nadu Forest Department]] was inaugurated on 31 January 2016 by former Minister [[M. S. M. Anandan]]. The Hall of Fame is now permanently at the Tamil Nadu Forest Academy, [[Coimbatore]]. In 2023, Tamil Nadu government has declared 7 October as Nilgiri Tahr Day in honour of him.<ref>{{cite web |title=Twitter Message of Tamilnadu CM |url=https://cms.tn.gov.in/sites/default/files/press_release/pr071023_2027.pdf |website=Tamilnadu Government |access-date=7 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=The Hindu Bureau |first=The Hindu |date=2023-10-06 |title=Tamil Nadu celebrates first Nilgiri Tahr Day |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/tamil-nadu-celebrates-first-nilgiri-tahr-day/article67390115.ece |access-date=2024-10-07 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>
